opening.argument: The presentation explains stimulus-check eligibility and payment timing while telling qualifying viewers that no application is needed: the IRS will send payments automatically using tax-return information. Its discussion of links and requests for personal information is a warning, not a request for viewers to act. The speaker says not to click an email link to claim a check, warns that a purported IRS call may seek bank-account and Social Security information, and cautions against websites promising faster payment. The description also identifies USCitizenshipTest.org as a private informational site unaffiliated with a government agency. Taken together, these are informational guidance and cautions, not a solicitation.

citations.quote: If you qualify for the check, there's nothing you need to do or apply. The IRS will automatically send you the check based on the information on your tax return.
You might receive an email asking you to click on a link to claim your stimulus check... Don't click it.
Or you might get a phone call from the IRS asking you to verify your bank account and social security number.
And don't go to any website and enter your personal information because it promises to get your checks faster!
